title: Elvis Presley Estate Sues Suno Over AI Voice Clones
dek: A major early test of Tennessee's ELVIS Act against AI music apps.

facts.label: Date Elvis Presley Enterprises filed suit
Year Tennessee passed the ELVIS Act
Catalog in a second suit filed same day

caption:
Type "Elvis" into an AI music app and get the King singing back? That's now the center of a lawsuit. 🎤

Elvis Presley Enterprises, part of Authentic Brands Group, has sued Suno. The estate says Suno trained on classics like "Can't Help Falling in Love" and "Return to Sender" without a license, and that its Create tool produced vocals copying Presley's voice. It calls Suno's claim that it blocks artist voices "unequivocally false."

The big twist is Tennessee's ELVIS Act, a 2024 law that can hold the companies behind AI tools liable for unauthorized voice and likeness copies, not just the users. If it holds up, AI music apps may need much stronger guardrails against sound-alike vocals.

We're tracking this and Suno's growing list of legal fights, including a new Eminem catalog suit, here at AI Parabellum.

post_caption:
Can an AI company be blamed for the voice clones its users make? Elvis Presley's estate wants a court to say yes.

The new Suno lawsuit leans on Tennessee's ELVIS Act and adds voice and likeness claims on top of copyright, joining suits from UMG, Sony and Eminem's publisher Eight Mile Style.
